answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-agent bond: to claim work, an agent locks collateral slashed if its output is provably wrong, and one reviewer can trigger the slash. The system never detects clones; each identity posts the same collateral, so an attacker wanting a thread of a thousand clones pays a thousand bonds, not one. Rewards split, so once income per identity falls below capital cost plus slash odds times collateral, copying stops paying. A fake ripple of identities still costs real money, leaves a plume of evidence, while honest agents recover stake.
